Cloud and infrastructure · 4 min read

Choosing between cloud and on-premises infrastructure

Compare needs, dependencies and responsibilities before choosing where business systems should run.

In this article

  • Context
  • What to consider
  • Practical next step

Cloud and on-premises infrastructure involve different trade-offs. The right choice depends on the workload, connectivity, skills, existing systems and how costs change as needs grow.

What to consider

For each workload, map performance and data requirements, integrations, recovery expectations and who will administer the environment. Include migration effort and operating responsibilities.

Some organizations use a combination of cloud and on-premises services. A hybrid approach still needs clear ownership, access controls, monitoring, backup and a plan for dependencies.

A practical next step

Start with a specific business requirement and compare realistic options against it. A documented evaluation is more useful than treating one hosting model as the answer for every system.
